items.summary: Large language model serving is limited by facility power. Energy per token determines how many tokens a datacenter can serve, while a latency target bounds how quickly each user receives them. During decode, every weight is read from memory for every generated token. Batching amortizes this read across users but makes no individual user faster. Speculative decoding does: a drafter proposes several future tokens, and the target model verifies them in a single forward pass that reuses the same weight read. Because every drafted token must be verified whether or not it is accepted, the energy speculation saves depends on how many drafted tokens are accepted. This saving is hard to pin down. It varies across target models from different attention families and across drafting schemes, and it depends on the text being served. Every drafter we evaluate accepts fewer tokens on conversation than on code, and every trained drafter accepts fewer on Romansh, a low-resource language, than on English. We measure speculative decoding under production serving conditions (SGLang, CUDA graphs enabled) on H100 and H200 GPUs, at batch sizes up to 64 across 5 corpora. On dense models, verification, not drafting, dominates the energy cost. The saving shrinks as the batch grows, because batching has already shared the weight read that speculation would divide among the accepted tokens. At large batch sizes, block drafters push verification past the balance point between arithmetic and memory traffic into the compute-bound regime, where the saving becomes a loss, and a drafter with low acceptance raises energy per token. Meeting a tighter latency target with speculation then costs additional energy. Larger batches lower energy per token without speculation. Speculation adds to that saving only when acceptance is high, and on the model we tested it leaves little headroom for latency-preserving DVFS.
items.title: Only Accepted Tokens Count: An Energy Accounting of Speculative Decoding Under Latency Targets

items.summary: Altermagnets combine compensated collinear magnetic order with momentum-dependent nonrelativistic spin splitting, offering new opportunities for spintronic applications. Here, we propose a route to optically induce altermagnetism through coherent lattice control. Using symmetry analysis, we identify phonon distortions that lift the spin degeneracy of conventional antiferromagnets while preserving the rotational symmetries connecting opposite-spin sublattices. Among these, geometric chiral phonons provide a particularly appealing pathway, linking the emergence of altermagnetism to structural chirality. Taking Fe$_2$TeO$_6$ as a prototype, we demonstrate that a linearly polarized mid-infrared pulse can drive a structural instability through negative biquadratic coupling between an infrared-active phonon and an optically silent, symmetry-breaking mode. First-principles-based lattice dynamics reveal the emergence of a transient chiral distortion, while electronic-structure calculations establish that the light-induced structure exhibits nonrelativistic spin splitting characteristic of altermagnetism. Our results establish a symmetry-guided pathway toward the ultrafast optical control of altermagnetic states through nonlinear phononics.
items.title: Light-induced chiral altermagnets from conventional antiferromagnets

items.summary: Alignment is not a constraint imposed on an artificial agent; it is the practical expression of what an artificial intelligence is, an artefact dependent upon ends it does not originate. That inference, from a premise the philosophy of mind already supplies to a conclusion that the ethics of robotics and recent magisterial teaching have reached by other routes, is the paper’s principal contribution. The “nurtured consciousness” of the title names a regime of formation, not a claim that machines are conscious; the argument rests on intentionality alone. The paper develops that inference as the Causal Provenance Doctrine (CPD): an account, Aristotelian and Thomistic in its metaphysics, of all intelligence, human and artificial, as derivative of an intentional causal order, with intentionality passing from the divine intellect through human reason to artificial systems. Its premise, borrowed rather than new, is that artificial intelligence has only derived intentionality and so no telos of its own. From this follows the Severance Risk Hypothesis (SRH), the doctrine’s testable corollary: the risk of misalignment rises as a system’s effective objective loses traceability to the end its makers held. The relational school’s objection to intellect-centred readings of the image of God is answered with a single distinction: a faculty can be out-performed, a participation cannot. The argument is theological at its root. A secular reader can reach the derived-intentionality claim and the account of responsibility that follows from it, at the price of a realist distinction between substances and artefacts, but obtains from it no standard for judging the makers’ ends, which must then be brought from elsewhere. A common Catholic and Orthodox formulation follows: the traditions converge on its practical conclusions, locate the image of God differently, and differ on the neutrality of the tool in a way the doctrine proposes to resolve. An artefact whose intentionality is wholly borrowed cannot, by obscuring that provenance, become an agent with ends of its own; it becomes a malfunctioning instrument whose purpose has been corrupted. The paper includes two appendices: a comparative case for intentional causality with an illustrative scorecard (Appendix A), and a test design for the Severance Risk Hypothesis (Appendix B). Approx. 22,000 words including notes.
items.title: The Causal Provenance Doctrine: Nurtured Consciousness, AI, and the Architecture of Intent

items.summary: Transformer-based architectures have revolutionized Question Answering (QA), yet navigating the trade-off between architectural complexity, computational efficiency, and robust generalization remains a critical challenge. This study presents a rigorous, side-by-side evaluation of four distinct Transformer models—ALBERT, RoBERTa, DeBERTa, and XLNet—on the SQuAD v2.0 benchmark, which demands both precise span extraction and calibration to abstain from unanswerable queries. By employing identical preprocessing pipelines and hyperparameter schedules, we isolate the impact of specific architectural innovations, including dynamic masking, disentangled attention, and permutation language modeling. Experimental results establish RoBERTa as the performance leader (85.90% EM, 88.69% F1), validating the efficacy of robust optimization strategies. Notably, DeBERTa followed closely (85.41% EM, 88.54% F1) but achieved superior performance on unanswerable questions (88.24%), suggesting that its disentangled attention mechanism offers enhanced verification capabilities against distractor entities. XLNet demonstrated competitive potential (78.30% EM) via its autoregressive formulation, while ALBERT confirmed its status as the efficiency benchmark, delivering respectable accuracy (80.70% EM) with a fraction of the parameter footprint. Qualitative error analysis reveals that while lighter models are prone to "hallucinating" answers, advanced architectures primarily fail due to subtle reasoning errors rather than entity mismatch. These findings provide a definitive decision framework for practitioners: prioritizing RoBERTa and DeBERTa for maximum reliability in complex domains, and leveraging ALBERT for scalable, resource-constrained deployments.
items.title: Comparative Analysis of Transformer-Based Models for Question Answering on SQuAD v2.0

items.summary: An open benchmark for testing geochemical fertility indices for magmatic Ni-Cu-PGE sulfide deposits. items.summary: Physical reservoir computing leverages the rich dynamical response of non-linear physical bodies to process temporal information without electronic microprocessors. Tensegrity structures, networks of discontinuous compression struts suspended within continuous tension cables, exhibit exceptional compliance, multi-stability, and high-dimensional configuration manifolds, making them prime candidates for mechanical intelligence in extreme, radiation-heavy environments. However, current methodologies rely predominantly on heuristic evolutionary algorithms or brute-force trial-and-error to configure such systems, lacking a rigorous analytical design framework. In this paper, we bridge this gap by establishing an explicit, first-principles mathematical mapping between the internal self-stress null space of a tensegrity network and its Information Processing Capacity (IPC). By decomposing the tangent stiffness matrix into material elastic ($K_e$) and pre-stress geometric ($K_g$) contributions, we demonstrate that the computational memory and fading-memory time constants of a tensegrity reservoir can be systematically engineered by tuning member pre-tensions within an admissible convex cone, holding spatial geometry strictly constant.
items.title: Formally Verified Pre-Stress Manifolds for Dynamic Stability and Adaptive Physical Intelligence in Tensegrity Reservoir Computing

items.summary: LLM-based agents are increasingly used to complete complex, long-horizon tasks without human intervention. To make progress toward the task goal, agents need to perform different duties, such as planning and verification, when needed. To understand how single agents manage these duties during long-horizon execution, we conduct a preliminary study. Our analysis shows that verification has the strongest association with task success, but often occurs late, leaving limited opportunities for correction. We also find that the proportion of duty-relevant information decreases as records from different duties accumulate in a shared context. These findings lead us to examine whether multi-agent systems (MAS) can address these problems by assigning duties to agents with separate contexts. Our analysis shows that this separation alone is insufficient. Agents can lose track of the overall goal and repeat prior investigations. They may also lack necessary background while receiving irrelevant information from others. To maintain goal awareness and coordinate collaboration as task needs change, we propose Goal-Aware Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaboration (GAD). It uses a growing execution graph to organize subtasks and their dependencies. To keep agents focused on their goals, each context retains the original instruction and the assigned task's goal and acceptance conditions. To adapt collaboration and information sharing during execution, agents can divide tasks into subtasks and specify dependencies based on execution evidence. These dependencies guide when agents work and which results they receive. Verification and recovery check subtask results and full task completion against their goals, providing feedback for repair when checks fail.
items.title: Goal-Aware Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaboration for Long-Horizon Tasks

items.summary: We consider three-dimensional imaging of compactly supported anisotropic electric media from fixed-frequency polarimetric Maxwell far-field data. Maxwell transversality creates an obstruction absent from scalar Born inversion: each measurement determines only a projected action of the tensor-valued Fourier transform. We first resolve this obstruction by a finite-dimensional polarimetric inversion. For a general complex $3\times3$ contrast, three incidence--observation configurations are necessary, and we give an explicit three-configuration design that is sufficient at every nonzero interior Fourier point. Its Gram determinant yields quantitative conditioning information and exhibits the loss of recoverability at the boundary of the accessible Fourier ball. After tensor demixing, the inverse problem reduces componentwise to restricted Fourier inversion on the unit ball, which we regularize by spectral cutoff in three-dimensional ball generalized prolate spheroidal wave functions. For discrete acquisition, a combined reconstruction error estimate separates the effects of measurement noise, polarimetric amplification, off-grid Fourier mismatch, quadrature error, Born modeling error, and spectral truncation. Numerical tests examine polarimetric conditioning and use analytically generated Born data to compare three- and six-configuration recovery and assess off-grid sensitivity. Reconstructions from full-Maxwell volume-integral data assess the effects of noise, wavenumber, and basis choice, as well as the recovery of different tensor components.
items.title: Polarimetric Low-Rank Imaging of Anisotropic Maxwell Media

items.summary: Gravitational observations can leave material properties undetermined in two different ways: distinct states can have the same total source, and distinct spacetime histories can have the same retained observations. We organize these inverse problems in general relativity through a property-level identifiability criterion, with applications to stars and black hole candidates. Two ideal massless gases illustrate equal-source ambiguity: their temperatures differ by a factor of $(8/29)^{1/4}$ and their entropies differ while their stress-energy tensors agree. A separate causal-fluid example starts with identical sources and geometric data but different constitutive responses; the two models' curvature histories separate at linear order in proper time and their scale factors at cubic order. For black hole candidates, the relevant distinction is between stationary exterior parameters, perturbing fluxes and constituent history. The framework provides a test for whether retained data identify a material property, separating instantaneous source equality, history-wide source equality and observational projection.
items.title: Curvature Blindness: Material Inference in Stars and Black Hole Candidates

items.summary: We present posterior-landscape, a Python framework to identify and characterize morphological features in two-dimensional probability densities. The framework combines concepts from topological data analysis, statistical density-ridge estimation, and scale-space image analysis. It extracts localized concentrations, valleys, ridges, and changes of slope; for Bayesian reconstructions, it propagates uncertainty in feature recovery, geometry, and correspondence across posteriors. The framework also connects two-dimensional structures to features in one-dimensional marginals, and quantifies their correlation with other inferred parameters. We validate the method on controlled densities, and demonstrate its use on gravitational-wave population reconstructions, where it provides a systematic way to identify and interpret population features and assess which ones carry information relevant for cosmology. The resulting catalogues also offer a common morphological representation for future comparisons between predictions and population reconstructions.
items.title: posterior-landscape: morphological feature finding in two-dimensional probability densities

items.summary: As Large Language Model (LLM) agents increasingly participate in persistent social environments, understanding their long-term social interaction capabilities becomes increasingly important. While existing research has advanced long-term memory and conversational context retrieval, less attention has been paid to whether agents can autonomously re-engage with previously inactive conversations. In particular, remembering a past interaction does not necessarily mean that an agent can identify when to revisit it, decide to return, or reconstruct the context needed for a coherent continuation. To investigate this gap, we introduce agent social re-entry as a multi- dimensional evaluation problem, distinguishing three complementary capabilities: Finding, Returning, and Reconstructing. We develop a shared-snapshot evaluation framework that measures these dimensions independently, allowing us to examine how conversational resurfacing and persistent memory relate to different aspects of social re-entry. Evaluations across six LLM configurations show that resurfacing substantially improves target conversation identification, while persistent memory is associated with higher rates of autonomous target-directed replying. However, neither improvement is accompanied by consistent gains in contextual reconstruction. These results highlight the distinction between accessing previous conversations, choosing to re-engage, and maintaining conversational continuity. Our framework provides a way to evaluate these capabilities separately rather than relying on memory retrieval or conversational response quality alone.
items.title: Finding Is Not Returning, Returning Is Not Reconstructing: A Multi-Dimensional Evaluation of Agent Social Re-entry

items.summary: At high redshift, the cosmic microwave background (CMB) both cools relativistic leptons and provides seed photons for inverse-Compton (IC) X-ray emission. These two effects link the particle content of a bubble directly to the soft X-ray depression used to identify a cavity. We derive a physical criterion connecting lepton cooling, bubble volume, enthalpy evolution, and 0.5--2 keV X-ray visibility, while separating intrinsic filling of the X-ray depression from detector-dependent cavity recovery. For uncooled electron populations described by a power law with spectral index $s=2.5$, minimum Lorentz factor $100\leqγ_{\min}\leq1000$, and maximum Lorentz factor $γ_{\max}=10^5$, the measured atmosphere of the testbed high-redshift cluster SPT-CL J2215$-$3537 requires 0.6--1.2\% of the pressure in radiating leptons to fill the soft-band deficit. Across the full tested ranges of $s$, $γ_{\min}$, and atmospheric properties, the required fraction is 0.2--3.7\%. Complete loss of this component reduces the enthalpy by less than 3\% relative to an otherwise identical adiabatic bubble at the same pressure. A low-cutoff control with $γ_{\min}=10$ and $s=3$ instead requires 18.9\%, identifying the poorly constrained low-energy spectrum as the main physical uncertainty. For a fixed atmosphere and spectrum, the required fraction scales as $(1+z)^{-4}$. The declining-pressure tracks show that the X-ray deficit can cross the adopted detection threshold while the enthalpy deficit remains below 0.4\%; the time of this transition depends on the assumed pressure history. Thus, high-redshift cavity visibility depends on both the surrounding atmosphere and the pressure-carrying particle spectrum. This criterion provides the physical basis for an instrument-specific recovery analysis.
items.title: The Conditional CMB Visibility of High-Redshift X-Ray Cavities in Galaxy clusters

items.summary: Next-generation smart sensing devices necessitate on-chip integration of power-efficient reference circuits. The latters are required to provide other circuit blocks with highly reliable bias signals, even in the presence of temperature shifts and supply voltage disturbances, while draining a small fraction of the overall power budget. In particular, it is especially challenging to design current references with enhanced robustness and efficiency; hence, thorough exploration of novel architectures and design approaches is needed for this type of circuits. In this work, we propose a novel CMOS-only current reference, achieving temperature compensation by exploiting geometry dependences of the threshold voltage (specifically, the reverse short-channel effect and the narrow-channel effect). This allows reaching first-order temperature compensation within a single current reference core. Implemented in 0.18 μm CMOS, a version of the proposed current reference designed to deliver 141 nA (with 377 nW of total power consumption) achieved an average temperature coefficient equal to 194 ppm/°C (from −20 °C to 80 °C) and an average line sensitivity of −0.017%/V across post-layout statistical Monte Carlo simulations. Based on such findings, the newly proposed design methodology stands out as a noteworthy solution to design robust current references for power-constrained mixed-signal systems-on-chip.
items.title: A CMOS Current Reference with Novel Temperature Compensation Based on Geometry-Dependent Threshold Voltage Effects

items.summary: The framework models the physical vacuum as an uncompressed, dissipationless superfluid where elementary particles are localized solenoidal vortex dipoles rather than abstract mathematical points. Macroscopic leptons and baryons emerge as coherent closed rings and braided links formed by the superposition of these dipole elements. Universal particle identity and quantum entanglement originate from a single, space-filling primordial filament established prior to cosmic expansion. Because metric stretching exactly compensates for cosmological velocity damping, hydrodynamic circulation remains strictly conserved, preserving topological phase coherence across cosmic horizons and explaining Bell correlations without faster-than-light signaling. The Pauli exclusion principle and Fermi-Dirac statistics follow directly from continuum mechanics: vortex filaments cannot cross in an ideal fluid without an infinite energy barrier, and half-integer ribbon framing enforces an exact anti-symmetric exchange phase. The vacuum lattice is algebraically locked against turbulent shear and chaotic collapse by maximal Heegner class-number-one field arithmetic, establishing a regular discrete network protected by a positive spectral gap. Fundamental physical constants emerge as exact geometric invariants of this structure: The inverse fine-structure constant is the geometric aspect ratio of the fundamental leptonic vortex loop, locked by the node capacity of the discrete manifold and refined by lattice shear dressing. The proton-to-electron mass ratio derives from the six-fold coordination symmetry of the host lattice multiplied by the phase-space volume of a three-strand Borromean baryon braid under parity invariance. The electroweak mixing angle reflects the topological projection of three-dimensional space onto the terminal genus-zero modular curve, flowing under standard renormalization to experimental precision. items.summary: Weight-normalized (WN) training is emerging as a compelling alternative to conventional weight decay (WD), with recent studies reporting substantial pretraining loss gains. We show that these gains are driven primarily by the induced effective learning rate (ELR) trajectory rather than by normalization alone. Matching ELR trajectories largely collapses the training loss dynamics of WN and WD. Schedule design should therefore target ELR rather than the nominal learning rate (LR) alone. Building on this principle, we propose AIR (Affine Inverse-square-Root decay), which combines a theoretically derived $1/\sqrt{t}$ decay with an affine adjustment to satisfy prescribed peak and terminal LRs over a finite training horizon. We further identify late-stage ELR scheduling as a key source of its gains, because a shared late schedule attenuates the effect of earlier LR choices. Experiments on 128 B-token Mixture-of-Experts pretraining demonstrate that AIR outperforms cosine and other candidate schedules in training loss, downstream performance, and hyperparameter robustness, reducing terminal training loss by approximately 0.01 relative to cosine at matched cumulative LR. Applying the same ELR trajectory to WD reproduces the corresponding training dynamics, showing that the benefits extend beyond fixed-norm training and establishing ELR as the principled scheduling object.
items.title: Your LR Schedule May Not Be Principled: Effective Learning Rate Scheduling in Weight-Normalized Training

items.summary: The repository contains three datasets, related to the paper "Broadband Ptychotomography with a Hyperspectral Detector" (Physical Review Letters, 2025). The datasets are made available to interested researchers.  broadband_ptycho_NMC_raw_data.tar.gz : folder containing the raw data (9600 folders: 16 projections x 600 frames per projection). The folder also contains the file 20231203_223438_VDS_share.h5. This is a virtual dataset bringing together all the raw data in a legible format. The virtual dataset should point to relative paths within the folder (0000/data.h5, 0001/data.h5... where the numbers go from 0 to 9599). This VDS file contains the following datasets: /cube/cube, shape: 16 projections * 600 frames per projection * 2500 bins * 264 pixels * 264 pixels. Raw diffraction patterns, spectral bin width of 16 eV.  /cube/energies, shape: 16*600*2500 /integrated/counts, shape: 16*600*264*264. Diffraction patterns integrated along 2500 bins.  /integrated/energy, shape: 16*600*264*264.  /spectrum/counts, shape: 16 projections * 600 frames per projection * 4000 spectrum bins /spectrum/energies, shape: 16*600*4000 20231203_223438_7.53-8.81keV_16ener_16proj_share.h5.gz: compressed folder with raw data in a limited energy range (7.53 keV - 8.81 keV) in 16 energy bins (208 eV wide, 80 eV step size) as described in Stolp et al.  This data also contains motor positions retrieved from the hardware during acquisition. /cube/energies, shape: 16 32-bit float /data/frames, shape: 16*16*600*264*264 32-bit float. dim0 is energy, dim1 is rotation angle /data/scan, shape: 16*16*600*5 64-bit float. dim0 is energy, dim1 is rotation angle. dim3 contains the acquisition parameters [energy, angle, x, y, z] spectral_ptycho_reconstructions.tar.gz : compressed folder with all 16 reconstructed projections (h5 files). Each projection has 16 reconstructions at different energies.  Ptychographic reconstruction of the raw data was performed with PtyREX, a Diamond Light Source software package. The frame positions were calculated automatically knowing that each projection was acquired with 20 steps in y * 30 steps in x, where steps in y = 1 um and steps in x = 1 um, and x is the fast axis. "x" refers to the horizontal direction and "y" refers to the vertical direction.  When using the data, please cite W. Stolp et al, "Broadband Ptychotomography with a Hyperspectral Detector", Phys. Rev. Lett. 134 (10.1103/kbrf-gb9c) and acknowledge this repository.

items.summary: Gravitational observations can leave material properties undetermined in two different ways: distinct states can have the same total source, and distinct spacetime histories can have the same retained observations. We organize these inverse problems in general relativity through a property-level identifiability criterion, with applications to stars and black hole candidates. Two ideal massless gases illustrate equal-source ambiguity: their temperatures differ by a factor of $(8/29)^{1/4}$ and their entropies differ while their stress-energy tensors agree. A separate causal-fluid example starts with identical sources and geometric data but different constitutive responses; the two models' curvature histories separate at linear order in proper time and their scale factors at cubic order. For black hole candidates, the relevant distinction is between stationary exterior parameters, perturbing fluxes and constituent history. The framework provides a test for whether retained data identify a material property, separating instantaneous source equality, history-wide source equality and observational projection.
items.title: Curvature Blindness: Material Inference in Stars and Black Hole Candidates

items.summary: Financial AI systems must support decision-bearing questions involving payments, collections, cash flow, and compliance while ensuring numerical accuracy, traceability, and auditability. Large language models (LLMs) enable natural language interaction but cannot independently guarantee reproducible calculations or evidence-grounded recommendations. We present a production-grounded architecture integrating three components: a financial knowledge graph for enterprise relationships, temporal context, and provenance; a deterministic optimization engine for financial calculations and decisions; and a multi-agent LLM layer for intent interpretation, task orchestration, explanation, and claim validation. A coordination layer, termed context engineering, selects, ranks, composes, and validates query-specific context across ERP systems, tools, and tenants. Based on observations from 15 deployments over approximately 11 months, single-agent pipelines exhibited hallucination rates of about 7-9% (5-10% across query types), including invented invoices and unsupported financial claims. Graph-backed multi-agent validation reduced observed rates to below 1%, although these findings are observational rather than causal. ERP data quality and tenant-specific schemas remained major implementation challenges. Reusable mappings, graph templates, and validation policies coincided with a reduction in deployment time from roughly six to two weeks. We argue that financial context engineering extends beyond text-centric retrieval-augmented generation by requiring structured relationships, temporal validity, exact numerical evidence, access controls, and validation against source records and solver outputs. We outline research challenges in evaluation, reproducibility, privacy, context quality, and cross-tenant generalization.
items.title: Beyond LLM Wrappers: Context Engineering and the Three-Engine Architecture for Reliable Financial AI

To view all available pipelines, just search "warp" in the Dockstore search and browse the workflow list. See Dockstore documentation for details on launching the workflow. items.summary: Cardiorenal syndrome (CRS) is a complex condition involving bidirectional interactions between cardiovascular and renal dysfunction. Its pathophysiology includes hemodynamic abnormalities, venous congestion, neurohormonal activation, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and metabolic disturbances. This narrative review aims to analyze the mechanisms of CRS and assess the relationship between renal function and clinical prognosis in patients with cardiovascular diseases, focusing on mortality, heart failure hospitalization, kidney dysfunction progression, and treatment-related renal changes. The review synthesizes evidence from clinical guidelines, randomized trials, observational studies, and contemporary scientific publications, with particular attention to CRS classification, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), serum creatinine, albuminuria, biomarkers, and treatment outcomes. The evidence indicates that reduced eGFR, albuminuria, persistent congestion, and worsening renal function provide complementary prognostic information. An analysis of 3,715 EVEREST trial participants found that each 30% decline in eGFR was associated with an increased risk of death and cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. The DOSE trial showed that intensive diuretic treatment could improve fluid removal and symptoms while increasing short-term creatinine elevations. These findings highlight the importance of interpreting renal function changes alongside congestion, hemodynamic stability, baseline kidney function, and treatment response. Comprehensive cardiorenal risk assessment should incorporate renal function, albuminuria, urine output, cardiac biomarkers, electrolyte status, and clinical response to treatment. Further prospective studies are needed to validate integrated risk models in diverse patient populations.

items.summary: PHOTOSTABILITY OF BOTANICAL ACTIVES AND PACKAGING ENGINEERING AT THE LIMIT 中文書名:植物活性成分光穩定性與包材工程極限 Photostability of Botanical Actives and Packaging Engineering at the Limit is a 777-page English research working monograph investigating three coupled but independently falsifiable questions: photochemical degradation of identifiable botanical marker compounds, wavelength-resolved optical transmission through real packaging, and the qualification of storage safety against oxygen ingress and unknown photoproducts. Its central claim is conditional, not asserted. A package that retains more apparent active compound after simulated light exposure may simply exclude oxygen, reduce lamp heating, alter extraction recovery, or hide degradation products. items.summary: Financial AI systems must support decision-bearing questions involving payments, collections, cash flow, and compliance while ensuring numerical accuracy, traceability, and auditability. Large language models (LLMs) enable natural language interaction but cannot independently guarantee reproducible calculations or evidence-grounded recommendations. We present a production-grounded architecture integrating three components: a financial knowledge graph for enterprise relationships, temporal context, and provenance; a deterministic optimization engine for financial calculations and decisions; and a multi-agent LLM layer for intent interpretation, task orchestration, explanation, and claim validation. A coordination layer, termed context engineering, selects, ranks, composes, and validates query-specific context across ERP systems, tools, and tenants. Based on observations from 15 deployments over approximately 11 months, single-agent pipelines exhibited hallucination rates of about 7-9% (5-10% across query types), including invented invoices and unsupported financial claims. Graph-backed multi-agent validation reduced observed rates to below 1%, although these findings are observational rather than causal. ERP data quality and tenant-specific schemas remained major implementation challenges. Reusable mappings, graph templates, and validation policies coincided with a reduction in deployment time from roughly six to two weeks. We argue that financial context engineering extends beyond text-centric retrieval-augmented generation by requiring structured relationships, temporal validity, exact numerical evidence, access controls, and validation against source records and solver outputs. We outline research challenges in evaluation, reproducibility, privacy, context quality, and cross-tenant generalization.
items.title: Beyond LLM Wrappers: Context Engineering and the Three-Engine Architecture for Reliable Financial AI

items.summary: Mathematical supervision for language models is typically flattened into isolated problem-solution pairs, discarding the curricular organization and evidential structure of the original sources. We introduce TOME-Math (Textbook-Oriented Mathematical Evidence), a large-scale corpus that converts 2,118 textbooks spanning the core areas of university-level mathematics subjects into approximately 380K structured proof-supervision records while preserving chapter order, proposition-proof links, dependency references, and source provenance. Leveraging these structural signals, we explore curriculum learning across multiple mathematical subjects and characterize scaling patterns with supervision volume and source breadth. At full scale, fine-tuning on TOME-Math raises the unweighted mean score across our held-out evaluations and established public benchmarks by 16.7 percentage points over the base model, while exceeding all three public instruction-data baselines evaluated in aggregate. Our findings highlight structured textbooks as both a scalable source of mathematical supervision and an empirical framework for studying the impact of data organization on mathematical reasoning. We will release the corpus to facilitate further research on structured mathematical supervision.

items.summary: Gravitational observations can leave material properties undetermined in two different ways: distinct states can have the same total source, and distinct spacetime histories can have the same retained observations. We organize these inverse problems in general relativity through a property-level identifiability criterion, with applications to stars and black hole candidates. Two ideal massless gases illustrate equal-source ambiguity: their temperatures differ by a factor of $(8/29)^{1/4}$ and their entropies differ while their stress-energy tensors agree. A separate causal-fluid example starts with identical sources and geometric data but different constitutive responses; the two models' curvature histories separate at linear order in proper time and their scale factors at cubic order. For black hole candidates, the relevant distinction is between stationary exterior parameters, perturbing fluxes and constituent history. The framework provides a test for whether retained data identify a material property, separating instantaneous source equality, history-wide source equality and observational projection.

items.summary: Welcome to WARP WARP (WDL Analysis Research Pipelines) repository is a collection of cloud-optimized pipelines for processing biological data from the Broad Institute Data Sciences Platform and collaborators. The contents of this repository are open source and released under the BSD 3-Clause license . Table of Contents WARP Overview Navigating WARP Using WARP WARP Versioning and Releasing Testing in WARP Feedback Acknowledgements WARP Overview WARP pipelines provide robust, standardized data analysis for the Broad Institute Genomics Platform and large consortia like the Human Cell Atlas and the BRAIN Initiative. You can count on WARP for rigorously scientifically validated, high scale, reproducible and open source pipelines. Our pipelines are written as "workflows" using the Workflow Description Language (WDL) and they process a broad spectrum of "omic" and array-related datasets (see the overview table below). | Pipeline Category | Data Types | | --- | --- | | Germline Variant Discovery | Genomes, Exomes | | Genotyping Arrays | Variant discovery, Chip validation, Joint array analysis | | Single-cell/nuclei Transcriptomics | Droplet based (10x Genomics), Smartseq2 | | Single-cell Epigenomics | Single nuclei ATAC-seq, Single nuclei MethylC-seq | | Joint Genotyping | Genomes, Exomes | | Somatic Alignment (beta) | Exomes | Try our pipelines in Terra , a platform for collaborative cloud analysis! Learn how in the Using WARP section. Navigating WARP All versioned and released pipelines are in one of the three pipelines subdirectories: broad (pipelines for the Broad Institute's Genomics Platform), cemba (pipelines for the BRAIN Initiative) or skylab (pipelines for the Human Cell Atlas Project). Each pipeline directory hosts a main workflow WDL that includes a pipeline version number and a corresponding changelog file. Workflows may call additional WDLs, referred to as tasks, that are located in the tasks directory. Pipelines that are in progress or have not yet been validated are in the beta-pipelines folder. Using WARP There are three ways to use WARP pipelines: 1. Download the workflow and run on a WDL-compatible execution engine WDL workflows run on multiple systems, including Cromwell , miniWDL , and dxWDL (see the openwdl documentation ). To run a pipeline's latest release, first navigate to WARP Releases , search for your pipeline's tag, and download the pipeline's assets (the WDL workflow, the JSON, and the ZIP with accompanying dependencies; see Optimus example below). You can also access a pipeline's release page by selecting the pipeline version number at the top of the pipeline's README. After downloading the pipeline's assets, launch the workflow following your execution engine's instructions. 2. Run the pipeline in Terra Several WARP pipelines are available in public workspaces on the Terra cloud platform. These workspaces include both the WDL workflow and downsampled data so that you can test the pipeline at low-cost. If you are new to Terra, you can get started by registering with your Google account and visiting Terra Support . After registration, search for WARP-related workspaces with the "warp-pipelines" tag. To test the pipeline, clone (make a copy of) the workspace following the instructions in this Terra Support guide . 3. Run or export the pipeline from Dockstore Dockstore is a GA4GH compliant open platform for sharing Docker-based tools like WDL workflows. You can find WARP pipelines in Dockstore and run them on the Dockstore platform or export them to other platforms (including Terra). To view all available pipelines, just search "warp" in the Dockstore search and browse the workflow list. See Dockstore documentation for details on launching the workflow.
